correctness.rationale: The claim fixes the side-two cube, Haar normal U on S², intrinsic central section area and polygon side count. Coarea of three independent uniform coordinates yields A=4/a−(b+c−a)_+²/(abc) for a≥b≥c≥0; the face criterion is four sides iff a≥b+c. Ball equality normals are exactly the twelve two-coordinate diagonals. Near each one x=a−b,y=c give spherical Jacobian 1/√2+O(x+y) and a uniformly positive first-order deficit g=4x (y≤x), 2(y+x²/y) (y>x). Uniform radial error O(ε²) yields O(ε³) integrated remainder. Direct integration of cone regions yields areas 1/32 (quad) and (π+2)/64 (hex); 48 adjacent chamber sectors divided by 4π prove the two ε² constants and the conditional angular uniform law. Independently reconstructed 40 generic edge-plane intersection polygons and their hull areas against the analytic formula, max error 2.67e−15; a finite check only corroborates the analytic proof. Boundary normals have measure zero.

originality.rationale: Best-of-knowledge distinctive claim is the exact joint leading Haar near-max area/polygon-type constants and rescaled angular distribution, not Ball maximum or global cube-section side counts. Primary Melbourne–Roberto provides near-equality stability but no directional limit cone or sharp measure constant; Lonke studies unconditional face-count distributions; Ambrus classifies critical orientations. A published exact random box hexagon law is unconditional and mathematically cannot alone imply the area-conditioned limit. Unindexed stereological small-deficit formulas are a residual historical-priority risk.
